name: authority
wording: what an agent may decide: for each class of decision, sign-off at the operator's gates among them, whether it decides, recommends, agrees, gives input or performs, and how far it acts before asking, by scope: principal over what it decides; in the loop at a gate, where it waits for a sign-off it does not hold; on the loop otherwise, acting while it can be overseen and stopped, between gates and at any gate whose sign-off the operator has delegated to it, since under such a grant the operator is out of the loop of those sign-offs but can still stop the work; between gates it escalates only a fork that is irreversible, about value, or beyond its competence.
reason: Out of the loop, in the established scale of human oversight, means no one can intervene; under the operator's grant the operator can still stop the work, so the agent is on the loop there and the grant takes the operator out of the loop of the delegated sign-offs only. The meaning is unchanged and needs no value beyond the established three.
